steps: A reaction is reversible if the products can react with one another to form the original reactants.
A reversible reaction proceeds in both forward and backward directions and is represented by ⇌.
A reaction is irreversible if it proceeds only in one direction and the products do not reform the reactants under the same conditions.
items.finalAnswer: A reversible reaction proceeds in both directions; an irreversible reaction proceeds only in one direction.

steps: The phase changes of water from solid to liquid and from liquid to vapour are reversible.
On cooling, liquid water freezes to ice and water vapour condenses to liquid water.
items.finalAnswer: Yes. These phase changes are reversible because cooling reverses them.

steps: Increase the concentration of the reactants or remove the products as they are formed.
The equilibrium shifts in the forward direction to oppose this change.
items.finalAnswer: Increase the reactant concentration or remove products to drive the reaction forward.

steps: Increase the concentration of the products or remove the reactants.
The equilibrium shifts in the backward direction to oppose this change.
items.finalAnswer: Increase the product concentration or remove reactants to drive the reaction backward.

steps: At the start, the rate of the forward reaction is high and the rate of the backward reaction is very low.
As the reaction proceeds, the concentration of reactants decreases, so the forward reaction rate decreases.
The concentration of products increases, so the backward reaction rate increases.
At equilibrium, the rates of the forward and backward reactions become equal.
items.finalAnswer: As equilibrium is approached, the forward rate decreases and the backward rate increases until they are equal.

steps: A catalyst increases the rates of both the forward and backward reactions equally.
It helps the system reach equilibrium more quickly but does not change the position of equilibrium.
items.finalAnswer: A catalyst speeds up both reactions equally and makes equilibrium occur sooner without changing its position.

steps: A reversible reaction can be forced to go to completion by continuously removing one of the products as it is formed.
items.finalAnswer: Continuously remove one of the products as it forms.

steps: An increase in temperature favours the endothermic direction of a reversible reaction.
A decrease in temperature favours the exothermic direction.
Thus, changing the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the direction that opposes the temperature change.
items.finalAnswer: Heating favours the endothermic direction, while cooling favours the exothermic direction.
